scenarios.note: All required areas meet the floor with complete current observations, two independent paths each, current area/topology binding and sufficient dwell.
The work order is closed, but DMA-B's current conservative upper bound is below its service floor.
Values are above floor but DMA-A has only one independent measurement path.
All values appear above floor but DMA-A has not completed the stable dwell period.
A high weighted mean cannot compensate for DMA-C's known service-floor breach.
DMA-B's apparently normal signal is stale and cannot support restoration.
A required area has no observation; it cannot be omitted or imputed from another area.
DMA-B's conservative interval crosses the floor.
DMA-A has two device IDs but both paths share one gateway failure domain.
DMA-B cannot be bound to the current service-area/topology revision.
DMA-B is known to breach while DMA-C remains unknown; both conditions must be retained.
Measurements appear restored but the incident alarm remains active or unresolved.
A recurrence occurs after a previous restoration claim; the old claim cannot suppress the new breach.

interpretation_rules: Every required area appears exactly once in every scenario; a missing row is invalid, not an omitted obligation.
A known service breach requires current valid complete observation evidence; otherwise the result remains indeterminate.
An area above floor is only candidate_restored until two independent current paths and the stable dwell gate are satisfied.
Independent paths require distinct source families and must not share any active failed domain across physical interface, calibration, power, communications or clock.
Stale, failed, unverified or common-cause-dependent paths do not count as surviving independent evidence.
Stale or unverified service-area/topology binding cannot certify area-level restoration.
Work-order closure, operator statement, model estimate, cleared alarm or controller restart is not independent proof of service restoration.
A known breach and a separate unknown area must remain breached_with_indeterminate.
An active alarm or unresolved conflict blocks verified_restored even if measured values appear above floor.
A recurrence belongs to a new event lineage and cannot be suppressed by a prior restoration claim.
Aggregate weighted mean is diagnostic only and cannot override a required-area breach or unknown.
Potable-water quality, sanitation, health and regulation are outside this evaluator; hydraulic delivery does not imply safe water for use.
All IDs, metrics, values, paths, thresholds and timing constants are synthetic and non-normative.
claim_ceiling: Synthetic service-restoration semantic contract only. No physical repair, restored service, potable quality, health, regulatory or utility outcome is measured.
